messages:
maria-sre: Heads up — after the kernel rollout in us-west-2 last night we're seeing a handful of GPU nodes advertise 0 GPUs to the kube-scheduler. Symptoms: pods with nvidia.com/gpu requests are stuck Pending, cluster autoscaler not scaling, cost spike from fallback to on-demand.

sam-infra: Confirmed. Saw this around 03:10 UTC. Device plugin shows registration but allocatable goes to 0 right after driver module loads.

leo-mlops: Logs from node-27: 
```
Nov 03 03:09:45 node-27 kubelet[1234]: device-plugin: registered with kubelet
Nov 03 03:09:47 node-27 kernel: nvidia: probe of nvidia0 failed with error -2
Nov 03 03:09:47 node-27 device-plugin: detected 8 devices but driver-probe failed, setting allocatable=0
```

anya-eng: Could this be the new gpu-operator/deviceplugin image? We rolled 1.8.2 yesterday which changed probe ordering and adds the kernel taint handling.

maria-sre: I suspect the kernel headers we shipped (4.19 -> 5.15 backport) moved the nv-modeset module init ordering. Combined with the deviceplugin expecting nvidia-smi to be present early, the driver probe is intermittent. Also saw NCCL warnings in pods that did get scheduled: cross-version symbol mismatch.

sam-infra: Repro: boot node with old kernel + new operator = OK. New kernel + old operator = OK. New kernel + new operator = fail. So it's a timing/regression between operator/deviceplugin and kernel module init.

leo-mlops: Quick workaround: cordon affected nodes and restart the nvidia-driver DaemonSet on them to force probe after kubelet ready. Patch command I ran: 
```sh
kubectl -n gpu-system rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-driver -l operator.redwood.io/component=driver
```
That returned drivers to ready for ~70% of nodes.

maria-sre: Good call. For nodes that didn't recover I had to manually modprobe nv-host and then restart device plugin. Steps: 
```sh
ssh root@node-27 
modprobe nvidia
systemctl restart kubelet
# wait for device plugin registration
```

anya-eng: Filed an issue with the gpu-operator upstream. Summary: kernel taint/ordering + deviceplugin probe race causing allocatable 0 + NCCL ABI warnings. Linking logs and node diffs in the ticket.

deploy-bot: New issue created: #4123 "deviceplugin/driver probe race on 5.15 backport kernels" by anya-eng.

maria-sre: Ops notes for runbook: 
- Detect: kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.capacity,ALLOC:.status.allocatable
- If allocatable==0 and capacity>0: restart driver daemonset, modprobe nvidia, restart kubelet.
- If NCCL ABI mismatch: check driver version vs model runtime, fallback to earlier model variant or pause batch jobs.

sam-infra: Also adding a scheduler policy guard: temporarily prefer nodes in eu-central and us-east to avoid us-west rolling failures. Will open a routing rule to avoid spike in cross-region autoscaling.

leo-mlops: Cost note: fallback to on-demand and cross-region jobs added ~12% to this week's bill. Need a postmortem and a plan to pin kernel+driver combos in our fleet images.

maria-sre: Agreed. Plan: 1) pin gpu-operator to 1.8.1 until upstream patch, 2) lock kernel image for GPU nodes for next 3 weeks, 3) add a probe-retry loop to deviceplugin wrapper as a short-term hotfix.

anya-eng: I'll own the operator pin + ticket follow-up. Sam can you push the scheduler preference change and cost analysis?

sam-infra: On it. Pushing preference rule now and starting cost diff. :thumbsup:

maria-sre: Thanks all. Will update #incidents if anything changes.
